title: rules validate ships working in the shell estate and is declared-unimplemented in v3
body:
**A WORKING RULE VALIDATOR SHIPS IN THE SHELL ESTATE AND `intent claude rules validate` IS DECLARED-AND-UNIMPLEMENTED IN v3.**

`tests/unit/rule_validator.bats` drives a validator that walks the whole rule corpus and prints a per-rule `ok` / `error: ...` listing. It works: on 2026-08-30 it caught `IN-AG-FIAT-001` missing five required sections, within the hour of the rule landing, naming each section.

v3's equivalent refuses. Positive-controlled against a verb that certainly does not exist:

    intent claude rules validate    -> rc=2  "a known command that is not implemented yet"
    intent claude rules bogusverb   -> rc=1  "unrecognized subcommand"

Two exit codes, two messages -- so this is a PORT GAP, not an absence. **The register tracks declared-and-unimplemented as a state and that is the state this is in.**

**WHAT THE SHELL VALIDATOR DOES AND DOES NOT ENFORCE, measured rather than assumed.** It enforces the required section structure. It does NOT enforce the `concretised_by` clause: `IN-AG-RED-CONTROL-001` reports `ok` carrying zero entries against a schema requiring two. So porting it as-is would carry that hole across.

**WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND PARITY.** `intent/docs/rules.md` documents the validator's checks under a heading saying **"Run before every rule commit. The validator is fast"** -- a shipped doc instructing readers to run a v3 verb that refuses. The 2026-08-30 schema amendment added two more criteria to that list. So the doc's check-list is growing against a verb that cannot run it, and the only thing actually enforcing any of it is a bats test in the v2 tree that a consuming project never sees.

**SCOPE:** WP-06, CLI parity long tail. The shell implementation is the specification; the two unenforced schema clauses (procedural rules' `applies_when`, pattern rules' `concretised_by` >= 2) are new work rather than port work and should be named separately if they are wanted.
